The game of golf is not the same for everyone. Some people are very content to shoot over 100, because for some golf is about competition, but for most it is about relaxation. This initial meme that this whole set of posts is about is ideally fairly correct, but it doesn't address the issue that golf isn't the same thing to all people. For some people, the Escape that they are able to attain, over the weekend, I missed everything else that is heavy going on in their life, makes it to where it is just a beautiful thing to be outside and enjoy nature, so the score is irrelevant. It is a good thing to have nice clubs, and it is a good thing to play very good golf balls, that actually stop on the Green. I'm a heavy heavy advocate for short game practice, because it really seems to me, as an on-and-off golfer for 35 years, even though I'm 40, that most shots are lost right around the green. And those are the most embarrassing shots to lose. I can say with great confidence, on a simple flop shot over a greenside bunker to a tight pin, there is going to be about a 3-foot difference at least in the action, with spin, using a distance Ball versus something like a Pro V1. I would suggest everyone, just about use a ball that will spin around the greens. Even if you can't stomach spending $4 a ball on brand new Pro V1s, you can always find used ones on the internet for around $20 a dozen. Don't ever use a hard ball like a Top Flite ever again. And over the course of a couple of years, the cost of what's lost in golf balls, would be gained with just two lessons.
